en: *The Sutra on the Fundamental Vows of All Bodhisattvas*, one fascicle, translated by the lay practitioner Nie Daozhen of the Western Jin dynasty.
The Bodhisattva Prajñāśrī asked the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī: "By what causes and conditions does a bodhisattva [attain this]?"

In what way does one ensure that others cannot find fault with one's bodily conduct, that others cannot find fault with one's verbal expressions, and that others cannot find fault with one's mental thoughts?
For what reason does he not, in body, emulate the long or short [faults] of others; in speech, not speak of the long or short of others; and in mind, not think of the long or short of others?
"By means of this conduct of body, speech, and thought that he maintains, the multitude of Arhats, Pratyekabuddhas, as well as the devas and the people of the world, are unable to fathom or know it."
"In his bodily conduct, verbal expression, and mental thoughts, none can equal him, and none can cause him to waver;
in his bodily conduct, verbal expression, and mental thoughts, nothing can harm him;
in his bodily conduct, verbal expression, and mental thoughts, all are accomplished and fulfilled according to his will."
"The conduct of his body is pure, the speech of his mouth is pure, and the thoughts of his mind are pure;
the conduct of his body is without blemish, the speech of his mouth is without blemish, and the thoughts of his mind are without blemish;
the wisdom of his bodily conduct is supreme, the wisdom of his verbal expression is supreme, and the wisdom of his mental reflection is supreme."

"At birth he was handsome; at birth he possessed wisdom; at birth he practiced generosity; at birth he was well-born among his kin; at birth he was born into a noble family; at birth his complexion was beautiful; and at birth his auspicious marks were distinct from those of the multitude."
"Whatever the mind conceives is all powerful; it provides much protection and maintenance without forgetting, and is without any sense of attachment or stinginess.

His talent is lofty and his vigor is fierce; he is the most honored among the fierce, the most noble among the fierce, the most courageous among the fierce, the most valiant among the fierce, and peerless among the fierce."

"What is known cannot be measured; what is discussed has no limit, and what is discussed is incalculable, boundless, and unsurpassed. Their love for the Buddha’s sutras is all brought about by the diligent exertion of their past lives."
"In whatever matters he enters into or emerges from, people all trust and believe his words; there are none who do not respectfully submit to him;
in all that he does with his own body, there is nothing that is not pure and clean;
and among all the sutras he has examined, there is nothing he does not thoroughly understand."
"With single-mindedness, subdue the mind, and contemplate with clear understanding.

Turn the thoughts back to enter meditative absorption (*dhyāna*): enter into the midst of the five sounds; enter into the four matters; enter into the three matters; enter into the twelve matters; enter into the blessings, merits, and virtues produced in the past, future, and present; enter into the seven factors of enlightenment (*saptabodhyaṅga*); enter into the emptiness, impermanence, and non-obstruction; and enter into the sūtras of the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*)."
Fully endowed with mindfulness, goodness, loving-kindness, and compassion, their minds are entirely free from hatred or attachment.
They enter into the wisdom of the ten powers and are venerated by devas, Brahmās, Śakras, asuras, spirits, and nāgas.

"He protects all people of the ten directions—those who are terrified find refuge and liberation in him; those with urgent causes for fear find no one who does not grant them peace and security. He is luminous throughout the ten directions, like a lamp, like a torch, like a great fire, and like the sun and moon;
he carries people across the worlds, like a helmsman or a passenger on a ship."

"There is a Venerable Teacher who, among all the devas, the people of the world, and the wriggling and crawling creatures, is most virtuous and most noble; he stands alone as the most honored among the great assembly, a hero among heroes, supreme and without equal."
"How should one realize such a Dharma as this?
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva addressed Anaśrī Bodhisattva, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
That which the Son of the Buddha has asked is thus: out of supreme great compassion and for the sake of liberating many, you have made this resolve to inquire.
All that is asked pertains to the conduct practiced by the body of the Bodhisattva, the speech uttered by the mouth, and the thoughts conceived by the mind.
If one has the intention and mindfulness of the Way, all the merits of whatever deeds one performs can be fully attained, never increasing or decreasing.

When the Buddha preaches the sutras, all Buddhas of the past, future, and present receive and attain them; they all arise from this and achieve perfection; they cause all the people of the world to be entirely at peace and secure; all the sutras he speaks are received with truthfulness; all karmic evils from past lives are completely extinguished; all sutras are received and mastered; everything becomes delightful and excellent, such that there is nothing equal to it.
"In this way, O Son of the Buddha!
Those who practice the Great Way all attain it.
Regarding the household life of a Bodhisattva, he reflects in his mind, saying:
"May all people throughout the ten directions never again be bound by craving and desire, and may they all enter into the dharma of emptiness.
When a bodhisattva serves and makes offerings to their parents with filial piety, they think to themselves:
"May all people throughout the ten directions quickly attain the Way of the Buddha, so that I may deliver and liberate all people throughout the ten directions."
"When the Bodhisattva dwells together with his wife and children, he thinks to himself:
'May all beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions have all their cravings and desires completely extinguished.'"
"When a bodhisattva dwelling at home has a thought, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be liberated from the midst of craving and desire, and attain the ultimate transcendence of the Way.'"
"When a Bodhisattva dwells at home and engages in music for mutual enjoyment, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions listen to and receive the various sutras, and may they all be able to hear these teachings just as they hear this music being played.'"
"When the Bodhisattva puts on the seven treasures, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions be freed from their heavy burdens and may they all find rest.'"
"When the Bodhisattva was enjoying himself among the court ladies, he thought to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions be led entirely into the Buddha's scriptures and be uprooted from lustful excess.'"
"When the Bodhisattva was on the upper floor of the tower, he thought to himself:
'May all the people of the world in the ten directions ascend to this lecture hall of the Buddha’s sutras, so that they may all receive the various scriptures, such that none shall be their equal.'"
"When a Bodhisattva practices giving, they think to themselves:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world give away everything they possess to others, and may none have any greed or attachment. "
"When the Bodhisattva experiences the affection of love with his wife and children, he thinks to himself:

'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be enabled to escape quickly; may they completely cast off lustful excess and impure secretions, and cause them to awaken to and enter the void. "
"When the Bodhisattva feels weary and weary of being at home, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world attain liberation early, so that they are no longer bound or attached to anything.'"
"When a Bodhisattva leaves home to practice the Way, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions attain liberation; may they never again return to enter into the midst of craving and desire, and have nothing more to covet.'"
"If a bodhisattva, upon arriving at a Buddhist temple, thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be made to contemplate only the Buddha, so that they may all enter into all the sutras without any further hindrance.'"
"When the Bodhisattva arrives before his teacher and preceptor, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world ensure that whatever wholesome thoughts they harbor are never left unfulfilled, and may they all enter into the true scriptures.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sought to become a śramaṇa, he thought in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions reach their destination; may they all achieve fulfillment, and never again have regrets or stop midway.'"
"When the Bodhisattva departs from the life of a layperson, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world cause their merit to shine with supreme brilliance, and let none of them fall into indolence.'"
"When the Bodhisattva receives the kāṣāya, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions be free from defilement, and may they maintain their minds as the Buddha does.'"
"When the Bodhisattva shaves his hair, he thinks to himself:
'May the defilements of all people throughout the ten directions of the world be completely removed, and may I never again encounter them.'"
"When the Bodhisattva acts as a great śramaṇa, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions be led back to the *upāyakauśalyapāramitā* and may they all attain the sūtras.'"
"When the Bodhisattva acts as a śramaṇa, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions become śramaṇas, so that, like the Buddha, they may fully deliver all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions.'"
"When a bodhisattva upholds the precepts, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions likewise protect and uphold the prohibitive precepts, and never allow them to be transgressed against the Dharma.'"
"When a Bodhisattva receives a preceptor, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world cause those they know through dhyāna to transcend all limits, remaining entirely free from any hindrance.'"
"When a bodhisattva receives a teacher, they should think to themselves:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world cause whatever they do to be thoroughly practiced, and may they uphold the teachings as instructed without loss.'"
"When a bodhisattva takes refuge in the Buddha, they think to themselves:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions find joy in the Buddha-dharma and be reborn entirely in supreme and excellent realms.'"
"When a Bodhisattva takes refuge in the sutras, they reflect in their mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world ensure that none fail to attain the treasury of profound sutras, and may the wisdom they obtain be like the great ocean.'"
"When a Bodhisattva takes refuge in the Sangha, they reflect in their mind:

'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world find no one who does not obtain reliance and deliverance, just as the community of bhikṣus has that upon which they rely for deliverance and delights in the Buddha’s path and virtue.'"
"When the Bodhisattva opens the door, he thinks to himself:

'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world quickly open the gate of heaven and enter the gate of the Buddha’s sutras; may none turn back in weariness, but rather reach the path of the Buddha’s nirvana for themselves.'"
"When a Bodhisattva enters a room, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world attain liberation; may their dwelling places soon become like the dwelling place of the Buddha;
and may they soon attain the profound sutras that are beyond the reach of all Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas.'"
"When the Bodhisattva closes the door, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world cause the gates of the evil paths to be closed early, and may all the evils of their past lives be completely incinerated.'"
"When a Bodhisattva spreads out his mat, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world quickly enter into the most profound sūtras, and may they all perceive the people of the ten directions as empty space.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sits, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions sit in peace, just as the Buddha sits upon the lion throne; let not the mind have any attachment.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sits upright, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions enter into right merit, and let none harbor doubts or engage in the increase or decrease of the Buddha's scriptures.'"
“When the Bodhisattva breathes, he thinks in his mind:
‘May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions have their breathing stilled and attain contentment.
When the Bodhisattva turns his thought to observe, he thinks in his mind:”
"May all people throughout the ten directions of the world form this thought:
'I see the phenomenon of impermanence.
When the Bodhisattva rises from his seat, he thinks in his mind:"
"May all people throughout the ten directions of the world cause that which they perceive—the dharmas of empty space—to be fully understood by them.
When the Bodhisattva steps upon the ground, he thinks in his mind:
"May all people throughout the ten directions of the world abide in peace and security, never again to be shaken."
"When the Bodhisattva puts on the inner robe (nirvāṇa-saṃghāṭī), he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world gather and uphold meritorious virtues; may they all feel shame regarding all worldly possessions and quickly attain the Way of the Buddha.'"
“When the Bodhisattva fastens his belt, he reflects in his mind:
‘May all people throughout the ten directions bind themselves to all merits and cause them all to be firm.
When the Bodhisattva puts on his robe, he reflects in his mind:”
"May all people throughout the ten directions of the world cause their various merits to increase further, so that they may all enter into the various sutras and attain ultimate transcendence.
When the Bodhisattva puts on his saffron robes, he thinks to himself:
"May all people throughout the ten directions of the world always find joy in the Buddha's sutras, never being parted from them for even a moment."
"When a Bodhisattva holds a willow branch, he should think in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions study all the sutras and attain complete purity.'"
"When a Bodhisattva rinses their teeth and washes their mouth, they should think with a focused mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world have all their defilements and impurities completely purified, and may they abide in purity.'"
"When the Bodhisattva walks to and fro, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions abandon all evils, and sever lustful indulgence, anger, and ignorance.'"
"When the Bodhisattva reaches the water, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world cause the Buddha’s sutras to be entirely pure and clean.
When the Bodhisattva carries the water while walking, he thinks in his mind:"
"May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be made diligent and reverent, with gentle and good hearts and pure bodies.
When the Bodhisattva washes his hands, he thinks in his mind:
"May all people throughout the ten directions of the world have gentle and beautiful hands to grasp the various sutras, paths, and dharmas."
"When a Bodhisattva washes his face, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions enter the Way of the Buddha’s scriptures; may there be no blemish or impurity upon my countenance.'"
"When the Bodhisattva was about to go out the door, he thought to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions attain whatever they seek and strive for, and may they quickly obtain them without any further hindrance. "
"When the Bodhisattva is heading toward the Way, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world attain Buddhahood early, and never again be made to turn back.
When the Bodhisattva practices the Way, he thinks in his mind:"
"May all people throughout the ten directions enter into the bottomless sutras; may they all penetrate deeply into these scriptures, purify their bodies, and be free from all obstructions.
When the Bodhisattva walks up an incline on the path, he reflects in his mind:
"May all people throughout the ten directions take joy in the Buddha’s sutras, never reaching a point of weariness."
"When the Bodhisattva practices the Way while descending a slope, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions enter the Great Way of the Buddha and be fully permeated by all wisdom.'"
"When the Bodhisattva walks along a winding path, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions have no perverse thoughts, and may they not utter evil speech.'"
"When the Bodhisattva practices the straight path, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions direct their minds toward the right path, and may none harbor flattery or deceit.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees dust rising and filling the road, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be made to cast off all desires and always attain the clarity of the scriptures.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees dust covering the road, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world always possess gentle hearts and fully attain all forms of loving-kindness and compassion.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees a cool, shady tree, he thinks to himself:

'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions cause all unwholesome dharmas to be completely eliminated, and may they enter the Buddha's scriptures with proficiency and full awakening.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees a lecture hall or a vihāra, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world hear and receive these various sūtras, and may they all enter within them.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees the great trees of the forest, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world have no one who does not look up to, revere, and make offerings to me; may it be so for all those in the heavens and the world of men.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees the mountain, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world conceive thoughts of lofty talent and clearly understand all dharmas of merit, such that none may surpass them.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees a thorny tree, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions swiftly distance themselves from lust, anger, and delusion.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees a leafy tree, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions be covered by the Way, attain meditative concentration (dhyāna), and enter into samādhi.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees a flowering tree, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions adorn their bodies and attain the thirty-two marks.
When the Bodhisattva sees a fruit-bearing tree, he thinks to himself:"
"May all people throughout the ten directions attain both flowers and fruit, and may they all be fully endowed within the Buddha’s sutras.
When the Bodhisattva sees flowing water, he thinks to himself:
"May all people throughout the ten directions enter the deep pool of the flow of the Buddha’s sutras, and may they all attain the wisdom of the Buddha."
"When the Bodhisattva saw the well, he thought to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions quickly open the gate of the sutras, so that there is but one flavor without any difference.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees water being drawn from a well, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions be fully endowed with the wisdom of the Way, and may they enter into the dharma of meritorious qualities.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees a spring of water, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions who inquire about wisdom gain much understanding, and may they all gather within the Way of the Buddha’s scriptures.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees great water, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions come to fully uphold all dharmas of merit so that they are inexhaustible, such that at no time can anyone surpass them.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees a bridge, he thinks to himself:

'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions attain the ultimate crossing over by means of all the sutras, just as people cross over by means of a bridge, without there being a time when it comes to an end.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees a house, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be led far away from craving and desire; may I know all that is thought in the minds of the people of the ten directions.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees the garden, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions have minds free from attachment and clinging, and may they find no delight in the five kinds of music or the five objects of thought.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees a fruit garden, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions have no sorrow or anxiety in their hearts, and may they all attain the fundamental root of profound wisdom.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees a pleasure garden, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be such that none fail to practice diligence; may none be allowed to depart from the various sūtras of the Buddha.'"
When the Bodhisattva saw the great assembly departing in such splendor, he thought to himself:
"May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions be likewise adorned, and may they all attain the thirty-two marks of a Great Man."
"When a Bodhisattva sees someone who is sorrowful and anxious, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions never again experience sorrow and anxiety.
When a Bodhisattva sees someone who is joyful, he thinks to himself:"
"May all people throughout the ten directions of the world delight in the profound sutras.
When a bodhisattva sees someone who does not find joy, he thinks to himself:
"May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be free from attachment to affection and love."
"When a Bodhisattva sees people at peace, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions be made peaceful and secure, attaining a peace and security such as that of a Buddha.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees people undergoing diligent toil and suffering, he thinks in his heart:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world extinguish all their diligent toil and suffering, and may they all behold the true and correct Path.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees someone who is strong and healthy, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be strong and healthy, just as the body of the Buddha is currently strong and healthy.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees someone who is ill, he thinks to himself:

'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be made to contemplate impermanence; may they all enter into the void and reach the ultimate consummation within the Buddha's scriptures, never to return again.'"
“When a bodhisattva sees a person of handsome appearance, he thinks to himself:
‘May all people throughout the ten directions of the world come to love and delight in the Buddha’s sutras.
When a bodhisattva sees a person of ugly appearance, he thinks to himself:”
"May all people throughout the ten directions never fall into ugliness and wickedness.
When the Bodhisattva perceives the repayment of kindness, he thinks to himself:
"May all people throughout the ten directions repay their gratitude to all Bodhisattvas."
"When a Bodhisattva sees someone who does not repay kindness, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be free from stinginess and greed, and may I lead them all to show others the Right Path.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees a śramaṇa, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world receive all the sūtras and attain their ultimate mastery.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees a follower of other paths, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world cause the roots of all evils to be completely extinguished and exhausted, and may they reach the ultimate realization of all sutras.'"
"When the Bodhisattva saw the rishi, he thought to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world have their every aspiration fulfilled and all their undertakings successfully accomplished.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees a person clad in armor, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions likewise receive this armor and be fully endowed with the Buddha's scriptures.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees those who are dull-witted and slow, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions become wise and capable, and may their actions never fall into the midst of various evils.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees a sutra being preached, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world, upon hearing and knowing it, have no wisdom that they do not understand.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees a sovereign king, he thinks to himself:

'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions each attain for themselves the status of a King of the Sūtras, spontaneously turning the wheel of the Dharma and preaching the Way without ceasing.'"
"When the Bodhisattva saw the Prince, he thought to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world become sons of the Buddha, and may they always be born through transformation within the sutras.'"
"When a Bodhisattva encounters high officials, he thinks to himself:

'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be made clear in the profound sutras; may there be nothing among their inquiries regarding wisdom that they do not understand, resolve, and apply.'"
When a bodhisattva sees a subordinate official or a high-ranking administrator, he thinks to himself:
"May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions be made to contemplate what is right; may they not harbor evil, and may they never be led away from the bodhisattvas."
"When the Bodhisattva sees the city, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions have bodies that are peerless, and may they all be so virtuous that none can surpass them.'"
"When the Bodhisattva beholds the palace and its towers, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world find joy in clarity of mind, and may they always remember to encounter virtuous merit.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees one holding a mendicant’s staff (khakkhara), he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world always practice goodness, be looked up to by others, always desire to give to others, and teach others the Dharma of goodness.'"
"When a Bodhisattva holds his alms bowl, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world offer many gifts; may they receive all these offerings, and may they all enter into boundless merit.'"
"When the Bodhisattva practices transcending [the stages], he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions enter the realm of the Buddha-dharma, without ever being subject to forgetfulness or error.'"
"When the Bodhisattva arrives at the gate of a person's house, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions and under heaven reach the gateway of the Buddha’s sutras.
When the Bodhisattva enters within the gate, he thinks in his mind:"
"May all people throughout the ten directions enter into the wisdom of the Buddha.
When the bodhisattva has not yet received food, he thinks in his mind:
"May all people throughout the ten directions be free from obstacles and calamities, and may they all enter into the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra."
"When the Bodhisattva has not yet received food, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world never again fall into the evil realms of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, asuras, or other miserable states.'"
“When the Bodhisattva sees an empty bowl, he thinks to himself:
‘May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be made empty of craving and desire.
When the Bodhisattva sees a full bowl, he thinks to himself:”
"May all people throughout the ten directions and the world be filled with all merits.
When the Bodhisattva sees the bowl being offered of rice, he thinks in his mind:
"May all people throughout the ten directions and the world cause them to practice the affairs of the Buddha-way."
"When a Bodhisattva sees a person who possesses a sense of shame and remorse, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be such that there is not one who does not feel shame and remorse regarding sensual desire.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees those who lack a sense of shame or remorse, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world cause all the evil thoughts in their minds to be completely cast aside, so that there is none who does not possess compassion.'"
"When a Bodhisattva receives fine food, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world have their aspirations fulfilled without exception, and may their minds remain untainted.'"
"When a Bodhisattva receives coarse food, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world possess gentle and supple hearts, such that there is none who does not feel compassion.'"
"When the Bodhisattva eats his meal, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions be like those who eat the food of dhyāna, always satiated by the sūtras.
When the Bodhisattva tastes the flavors of his food, he thinks to himself:"
"May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be satiated with flavors, just as when flavors are transformed by the Buddha’s throat; may they all attain the Sutra named 'Ambrosia'."
"When the Bodhisattva has finished eating, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions have their endeavors fully accomplished and enter the ultimate depths of the Buddha's sutras.'"
"When a Bodhisattva speaks a sutra and recites a prayer of aspiration, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions and under heaven speak what they have learned without end, and may it all enter into the various profound sutras of the Buddha.'"
"When the Bodhisattva has finished preaching the sutra and reciting the dhāraṇī for the transfer of merit, as he departs, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions emerge from the three realms and, within the emptiness of impermanent form, all fully receive the wisdom of the Buddha.'"
"When the Bodhisattva enters the water, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions enter into the wisdom of the Buddha; may the past, future, and present be entirely equal.'"
"When the Bodhisattva bathes, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions wash away the defilements of their minds, and may they all attain ultimate illumination that reaches to the furthest limits.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees the heat, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions be made to distance themselves from this heat and pass beyond it completely.'"
"When the Bodhisattva sees the time of cold, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions become generals among men, attaining places of supreme clarity and coolness.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees one reciting the sutras, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world understand the contents of all sutras, fully seek after wisdom, and completely grasp and uphold all insights.'"
"When a Bodhisattva sees a Buddha, they think to themselves:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world be brought together with all Buddhas, their minds free from any obstruction.'"
"When the Bodhisattva looked up toward the Buddha, he thought in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world have their vision free from any obstruction, so that they may see the infinite reaches.'"
"When the Bodhisattva prostrates himself before the Buddha with his head touching the ground, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions and under heaven be unable to see the top of the Buddha's head, whether they be in the heavens above or the world below.'"
"When the Bodhisattva rose from his prostration and gazed directly at the Buddha, he thought to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world practice this sutra so that none may be their equal.'"
"When the Bodhisattva circumambulated the Buddha once, he thought to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions perform this most excellent act of circumambulation, and may they all ultimately be granted the clarity of the sutras.'"
"When the Bodhisattva circumambulated the Buddha three times, he thought to himself:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions always be courageous in their actions and never depart from the path of the Buddha.'"
"When the Bodhisattva extols the Buddha’s merits and majestic spiritual power, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world cause their deeds to become immeasurable merit and immeasurable majestic spiritual power, reaching the ultimate pinnacle of excellence.'"
"When the Bodhisattva washes his feet, he thinks to himself:

'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions attain the divine power of the Buddha’s mental flight, so that they are no longer hindered by anything and fully enter into its perfection.'"
"When the Bodhisattva praises the marks of the Buddha, he thinks in his mind:
'May all people throughout the worlds of the ten directions have their bodies fully complete, just like the body described in the Buddha’s sutras.'"
"When the Bodhisattva lies down or sits, he thinks to himself:
'May all people throughout the ten directions of the world no longer be bound by craving and desire, and may they be completely purified amidst their hardships.'"
"When the Bodhisattva awakens from sleep, he reflects in his mind:
'May all people throughout the ten directions and the world attain the wisdom of a Buddha and obtain the ten powers.
This is the path constantly practiced by the Bodhisattva."
"In this buddha-field of Śākyamuni Buddha, there are ten billion Śakradevendra Indras, all residing in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; each of them individually conceived the desire to invite the Buddha."

All the Śakra-devānām-indras prepared for the Buddha seven-jeweled lion thrones within the Purple-Green Hall of Righteousness; they spread upon these seats all the finest, renowned, and exquisite *karpāsa* fabrics of various colors and diverse patterns, and each provided them with magnificent, latticed canopies, all according to their own desire.
The Buddha immediately knew all of this.

By means of his supernatural power, he manifested emanated bodies that were all present outside the outer gates of Śakra-devānām-indra’s palace in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven throughout ten billion worlds.
In each of the Śakra-devānām-indra abodes there was one Buddha; in total, there were ten billion Buddhas, all accompanied by assemblies of bodhisattvas.
All the Śakra-devānām-indras were filled with great joy; they all came out to welcome them, paid homage to the Buddhas, and invited them to enter.
The Buddha then entered together with the bodhisattvas and took his seat within the inner canopy of the purple-blue main hall.
Each of the bodhisattvas likewise sat individually within a jeweled pavilion atop a lion throne made of seven precious gems, each upon a lotus flower.
The Buddha continued to remain in these ten billion minor lands, sitting together with the bodhisattvas, his majestic spiritual power unmoving.

Bodhisattvas from the ten directions came to the assembly in great numbers—Bodhisattva Tánméimóti, another Bodhisattva Tánméimóti, Śrīmātikā Bodhisattva, Kunāmātikā Bodhisattva, Duòyèmóti Bodhisattva, Shātúmóti Bodhisattva, Ruònámóti Bodhisattva, Shāzhēmóti Bodhisattva, Āgāmóti Bodhisattva, Shālāmóti Bodhisattva, and Sàhémóti Bodhisattva.
The Sūtra on the Fundamental Acts of All Bodhisattvas in Search of Buddhahood.
